arxiv-2109-05451.title: H2Opus: A distributed-memory multi-GPU software package for non-local operators
arxiv-2109-05451.creator: Stefano Zampini, Wajih Boukaram, George Turkiyyah, Omar Knio, David E. Keyes
arxiv-2109-05451.description: Abstract . Hierarchical ℋ 2 \mathcal{H}^{2} -matrices are asymptotically optimal representations for the discretizations of non-local operators such as those arising in integral equations or from kernel functions. Their O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) complexity in both memory and operator application makes them particularly suited for large-scale problems.

arxiv-2110-08968.title: Momentum-Space Spin Antivortex and Spin Transport in Monolayer Pb
arxiv-2110-08968.creator: Kaijie Yang, Yuanxi Wang, Chao-Xing Liu
arxiv-2110-08968.description: Abstract Nontrivial momentum-space spin texture of electrons can be induced by spin-orbit coupling and underpins various spin transport phenomena, such as current-induced spin polarization and spin Hall effect. In this work, we find that a nontrivial spin texture, spin antivortex, can appear at certain momenta on the Γ − K \Gamma-K line in 2D monolayer Pb on top of SiC.

arxiv-2301-09570.title: A Novel Power-optimized CMOS sEMG Device with Ultra Low-noise integrated with ConvNet (VGG16) for Biomedical Applications
arxiv-2301-09570.creator: Ahmed Ayman, Mohamed Sabry
arxiv-2301-09570.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ahmed Ayman, Mohamed Sabry. The needle bio-potential sensors for measuring muscle and brain activity need invasive surgical targeted muscle reinnervation (TMR) and a demanding process to maintain, but surface bio-potential sensors lack clear bio-signal reading (Signal-Interference). In this research, a novel power-optimized complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) Surface Electromyography (sEMG) is developed to improve the efficiency and quality of captured bio-signal for biomedical application: The early diagnosis of neurological disorders (Dystonia) and a novel compatible mind-controlled prosthetic leg with human daily activities.

arxiv-2305-05923.title: Inhomogeneous deformations of Einstein Solvmanifolds
arxiv-2305-05923.creator: Adam Thompson
arxiv-2305-05923.description: Abstract . For each non-flat, unimodular Ricci soliton solvmanifold ( 𝖲 0 , g 0 ) (\mathsf{S}_{0},g_{0}) , we construct a one-parameter family of complete, expanding, gradient Ricci solitons that admit a cohomogeneity one isometric action by 𝖲 0 \mathsf{S}_{0} . The orbits of this action are hypersurfaces homothetic to ( 𝖲 0 , g 0 ) (\mathsf{S}_{0},g_{0}) .

arxiv-2402-19016.title: SPriFed-OMP: A Differentially Private Federated Learning Algorithm for Sparse Basis Recovery
arxiv-2402-19016.creator: Ajinkya K Mulay mulay@purdue.edu, Xiaojun Lin linx@ecn.purdue.edu
arxiv-2402-19016.description: Abstract Sparse basis recovery is a classical and important statistical learning problem when the number of model dimensions p p is much larger than the number of samples n n . However, there has been little work that studies sparse basis recovery in the Federated Learning (FL) setting, where the client data’s differential privacy (DP) must also be simultaneously protected.

arxiv-2406-17591.title: DocParseNet: Advanced Semantic Segmentation and OCR Embeddings for Efficient Scanned Document Annotation
arxiv-2406-17591.creator: Ahmad Mohammadshirazi, Ali Nosrati Firoozsalari, Mengxi Zhou, Dheeraj Kulshrestha, Rajiv Ramnath
arxiv-2406-17591.description: Abstract Automating the annotation of scanned documents is challenging, requiring a balance between computational efficiency and accuracy. DocParseNet addresses this by combining deep learning and multi-modal learning to process both text and visual data. This model goes beyond traditional OCR and semantic segmentation, capturing the interplay between text and images to preserve contextual nuances in complex document structures.

arxiv-2408-04870.title: ConfusedPilot : Confused Deputy Risks in RAG-based LLMs
arxiv-2408-04870.creator: Ayush RoyChowdhury † , Mulong Luo †1 , Prateek Sahu †2 , Sarbartha Banerjee †2 , and Mohit Tiwari †‡1
arxiv-2408-04870.description: Abstract Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a process where a large language model (LLM) retrieves useful information from a database and then generates the responses. It is becoming popular in enterprise settings for daily business operations. For example, Copilot for Microsoft 365 has accumulated millions of businesses. However, the security implications of adopting such RAG-based systems are unclear.

arxiv-2412-13901.title: Boundary values via reproducing kernels: The Julia-Carathéodory theorem
arxiv-2412-13901.creator: Frej Dahlin
arxiv-2412-13901.description: Abstract Given a reproducing kernel k k on a nonempty set X X , we define the reproductive boundary of X X with respect to k k . Furthermore, we generalize the well known nontangential and horocyclic approach regions of the unit circle to this new kind of boundary.

arxiv-2506-19772.title: Self-assembled clusters of mutually repelling particles in confinement
arxiv-2506-19772.creator: P. D. S. de Lima, R. De La Cour, K. Gaff, J. M. de Araújo, S. J. Cox, M. S. Ferreira, S. Hutzler
arxiv-2506-19772.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by P. D. S. de Lima, R. De La Cour, K. Gaff, J. M. de Araújo, S. J. Cox, M. S. Ferreira, S. Hutzler. Mutually repelling particles form spontaneously ordered clusters when forced into confinement. The clusters may adopt similar spatial arrangements even if the underlying particle interactions are contrastingly different.

arxiv-2510-22515.title: An End-to-End Generative Diffusion Model for Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2510-22515.creator: \firstname Jing-An \lastname Sun, \firstname Li \lastname Yan \fnsep, \firstname Charles \lastname Gale, \firstname Sangyong \lastname Jeon
arxiv-2510-22515.description: Abstract Heavy-ion collision physics has entered the high precision era, demanding theoretical models capable of generating huge statistics to compare with experimental data. However, traditional hybrid models, which combine hydrodynamics and hadronic transport, are computationally intensive, creating a significant bottleneck. In this work, we introduce DiffHIC, an end-to-end generative diffusion model, to emulate ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

arxiv-2601-05368.title: MOSAIC-GS: Monocular Scene Reconstruction via Advanced Initialization for Complex Dynamic Environments
arxiv-2601-05368.creator: Svitlana Morkva 1 Maximum Wilder-Smith 1 Michael Oechsle 2 Alessio Tonioni 2 Marco Hutter 1 Vaishakh Patil 1 1 ETH Zürich 2 Google {smorkva, mwilder, mahutter, patilv}@ethz.ch {michaeloechsle,alessiot}@google.com
arxiv-2601-05368.description: Abstract We present MOSAIC-GS, a novel, fully explicit, and computationally efficient approach for high-fidelity dynamic scene reconstruction from monocular videos using Gaussian Splatting. Monocular reconstruction is inherently ill-posed due to the lack of sufficient multiview constraints, making accurate recovery of object geometry and temporal coherence particularly challenging.

pmc-12359967.title: Heterologous expression of the M. abscessus CBASS system confers phage TM4 resistance in M. smegmatis
pmc-12359967.creator: Chun-Liang Wang, Ao-Fei Duan, Da-min Pan, Yi-Ou Zhao, Jian Yang, Yi-Cheng Sun
pmc-12359967.description: Phage therapy for multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus is constrained by the narrow lytic spectrum of phages due to unknown antiphage mechanisms. Bacteria deploy various defense strategies to prevent phage infection, but few have been comprehensively characterized in mycobacteria. Mycobacteriophage TM4 successfully delivers DNA into M. abscessus but fails to establish infection.

pmc-13148913.title: Swine reporter model for preclinical evaluation and characterization of gene delivery vectors
pmc-13148913.creator: Jarryd M. Campbell, Derek M. Korpela, Hesong Han, Sheng Zhao, Dennis A. Webster, Yen Anh H. Nguyen, Nicholas Koes, Robyn O. Aune, Hinsoukpo Dagan, Rebecca Milliken, Jonathan K. Watts, Niren Murthy, Daniel F. Carlson
pmc-13148913.description: Delivery of gene therapy vectors efficiently targeted to any somatic cell remains a key barrier for the development of genetic medicines. While rodent models provide insights into vector biodistribution and cellular tropism, their anatomical and physiological differences from humans limit their translational potential and studies in large animal models are often required.
